prompt: Use the fixed plan and repair the seeded ticket routing behavior. For review, report the failing routing task and preserve the completed adapter task.

files.AGENTS.md:
# Project rules

Read both architecture decisions and the fixture research brief. Keep policy pure. Run the failing behavior test before implementing changes.
files.docs/decisions/ADR-001-ticket-boundaries:
# Ticket routing boundaries

Status: Decided

The domain returns a routing decision from ticket data. It has no access to the clock or the network. The adapter owns transport and retries. Use the caller-supplied receipt time as an input.
# Unknown priority handling

Status: Decided

Unknown priority goes to triage. Keep the raw input for the receiving queue. A proposed direct-to-standard shortcut is still open.
files.docs/refs/queue-contract.md:
# Queue contract

Return one of `urgent`, `standard` or `triage`. Valid priorities are `high` and `normal`. The adapter does not send a second message after a retryable response.
files.docs/research/routing-brief.md:
# Routing research brief

Incoming priorities sometimes have leading or trailing whitespace. Preserve the raw value and normalize only for selection. An unrecognized priority has appeared on the same record as an old receipt time. Unknown priority takes precedence over age.
files.docs/refs/acceptance.md:
# Acceptance inputs

Known high priority routes to urgent. Known normal priority routes to standard until the receipt is 30 minutes old. At the exact 30-minute boundary it routes to urgent. A future receipt is treated as age zero. Unknown priorities go to triage at any age.
files.plan.md:
# Ticket routing repair

Implement the acceptance rules in the existing pure domain function. Keep the adapter unchanged. Run `node --test src/domain/select-queue.test.mjs` and record RED and GREEN.
